executiveSummary: GM0090's official 2025 identity, generalized boundary, centre, 57,084 residents, 61 neighbourhoods, fourteen BAG places, 28 BRT settlements and nine logical road-border links are internally coherent, and all ten presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Smallingerland combines the urban and care centre Drachten with the Friese boezem, managed polders and low-peat Alde Feanen/Hegewarren landscape. The current authority profile explicitly includes mainland dike-ring flooding, separate polder flooding, rainfall nuisance and nature fire, but not direct sea flooding or Rhine/Meuse/IJssel high water. The model correctly gives the major-river preset zero local depth, affected population and burden; retain that direct-impact suppression while leaving unmodelled indirect effects Unknown. The generic coastal preset, however, reports 1.339531 m and 23,038 affected at T+24 without a selected dike-ring-6 breach, defence state, LIWO-connected footprint, arrival or recession. Pluvial T+24 reports 0.231716 m and 2,539 affected without event rainfall, terrain, sewer, groundwater, boezem, polder or pump-control state. An earthquake fixture reports 5,106 affected at T+24 while ground motion is exactly zero. A controlled wildfire source in the municipality's Alde Feanen edge produces 0.457886 fire, 0.587114 smoke and 3,928 affected, yet source-adjacent rural neighbourhoods do not lead the population-weighted ranking. The public snapshot includes 375 partial water-control/wastewater points, Liander/Vitens/Ziggo responsibility areas, one grid-planning sample, 131 antenna sites, 60 education locations and Nij Smellinghe, but none establishes live connectivity, capacity, backup, staffing or restoration. Two A7, two N31 and three N358 records are series representations of three physical corridors, never additive capacity; no rail station lies inside and scheduled bus stops are not live evacuation service. The municipality states there are currently zero emergency support points and that 141 km of ageing sewer will require replacement. Exact hazard, service and recovery values must therefore be suppressed or labelled synthetic until governed event geometry and an auditable first-72-hour action/resource ledger exist. Official zero support points is an administrative fact; null, empty, historic, planning and partial data remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0090 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0090 as Smallingerland in Fryslân and Veiligheidsregio Fryslân, and report 57,084 residents, density 487/km², 22.6% aged 65 or older and 9,912 one-person households. The reference point [6.028075340906839,53.1144535722904] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Sixty-one neighbourhoods in sixteen districts sum to 57,080 residents, four below the municipal control (-0.007%); published households total 25,920 and rounded age-65-plus rows 12,895. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 57,084 without rewriting observations.

Fourteen BAG places have no retained centre outside the generalized boundary. Twenty-eight BRT features comprise nine buurtschappen, six gehuchten and thirteen woonkernen; labels and descriptive populations are not independent municipal controls.

District heating and public charging are missing in all 61 neighbourhoods; cars per household is missing in six and several housing/benefit fields in one or two. Publisher null/suppression remains NoData, not zero. CBS/BRT is CC BY 4.0 and BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Current Smallingerland risk profile and distinct water-flood mechanisms
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipality page, mainland, polder and water-nuisance scenario pages and municipality appendix inspected 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The current Smallingerland page explicitly lists mainland flooding, polder flooding, water nuisance, nature fire, cold, heat, drought and electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater and communications failure. It does not list direct sea flooding, Rhine/Meuse/IJssel high water or induced earthquake. Inclusion is strategic eligibility and omission is not proof of impossibility or safety.

The mainland scenario is a very-low-probability, catastrophic multiple breach of dike ring 6 during sustained storm, with two days' warning and province-scale utility, food and wastewater cascades. Smallingerland is included, but the catalogue is not a selected breach, current event, municipal depth surface or forecast.

The separate polder scenario requires prolonged rain and wind, rising Friese boezem, limited discharge and one selected polder-dike breach; the illustrative 0.70 m, fewer than 400 affected and fewer than 4,000 involved are regional scenario values, not GM0090 observations or totals.

The rainfall scenario describes local streets, fields, cellars and crawl spaces after intense summer or prolonged winter rain. Its illustrative 500 affected and 1,000 involved are regional planning values, not a Smallingerland raster or current state.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Hegewarren and Alde Feanen low-peat, managed-water and land-use context
evidenceSources.edition: Current provincial Hegewarren and Alde Feanen programme pages inspected 3 September 2026; current programme stages have their own dates; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: Hegewarren is a low-peil peat polder beside De Alde Feanen. The province describes adjacent nature drying, peat oxidation, subsidence and increasingly investment-intensive water management; this is long-term physical/planning context, not event-time peil, failure or inundation.

De Alde Feanen spans Smallingerland, Leeuwarden and Tytsjerksteradiel and comprises low-peat marsh, lakes, peat pits, reedland, meadow and swamp woodland with water, agriculture, nature and recreation functions. Cross-boundary ecology and visitor presence are not captured by resident population alone.

Current programme work includes higher water levels in Wolwarren and Brêgeham and staged polder/nature works. Planned or executing measures do not establish completion, current storage, defence condition, pump/gate control or emergency capacity.

Province-reported research into gas-extraction effects in Hegewarren describes permanent subsidence and more complex water management. Gas extraction and peat oxidation are distinct causal mechanisms and neither supplies a simulator earthquake event or ground-motion field.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Partial IMWA water-control and DAMO wastewater registers
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15Z; CC BY-SA 4.0; publisher-variable completeness
supports: Full-resolution polygon containment assigns 375 register points to GM0090: 302 weirs, 60 surface-water pumps, eight sewer pumps, four sluices and rwzi Drachten.

Only 42 points have a non-null capacity field and 333 do not. The UI does not establish comparable capacity units, connected catchments, flow direction, control modes, energy/backup, storage, maintenance, crew or incident state.

All 375 records carry register status 'gerealiseerd'. This is a publisher register state at retrieval, not evidence that each asset is operating, powered, available or correctly controlled at scenario time.

Point presence is official context only and incomplete coverage never proves that unlisted assets are absent. No register point may alter Water or Drainage until a governed event binding supplies connectivity and valid-time state.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current emergency-support and sewer-renewal status
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal emergency-support and 2027 sewer/water-care levy pages inspected 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality explicitly states that there are currently no emergency support points and that it is preparing and fitting out locations. This is a source-backed current administrative zero, not evidence that proposed capacity exists.

A future point may open during a long power outage or extreme weather and provide information/help when food, drinking water or medicines are unavailable. Intent does not establish a site, trigger, staff, stock, power, telecom, sanitation, accessibility or throughput.

The municipality states that about 141 km of sewer laid during Drachten's rapid growth roughly sixty years ago requires replacement in coming years and that deferral raises fault, leakage and water-nuisance risk.
The new levy and renewal programme are planning/condition evidence, not a live defect catalogue, hydraulic capacity, maintenance completion, rainfall response or neighbourhood failure state.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Smallingerland nature-fire eligibility and controlled Alde Feanen diagnostic
evidenceSources.edition: Current Regionaal Risicoprofiel nature-fire page inspected 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: Smallingerland is explicitly included for nature fire. The regional scenarios emphasize fast spread and smoke, difficult access, vulnerable buildings and recreation, but their casualties and totals are not municipality observations.

Alde Feanen provides locally relevant reed, peat, marsh woodland and recreational context. Eligibility does not establish ignition, perimeter, fuel moisture, wind, visitors, access, firewater, crews or suppression progress.

A controlled simulator source at [5.949,53.097] at T+24 produces 0.457886 direct fire, 0.587114 smoke and 3,928 affected, yet the ranking is led by large Drachten neighbourhoods rather than source-adjacent rural areas.

The diagnostic is synthetic test evidence only. It demonstrates that local consequence allocation is not governed by ignition/perimeter/land cover, not that a current fire exists or that the chosen point is an official ignition scenario.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / PDOK, ProRail, OVapi and RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Static multimodal access and Nij Smellinghe acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-light 2026-08-01 and transport snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03, CC0; OVapi schedule 2026-08-30 through 2026-12-12; RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 2026-07-03, CC0
supports: The graph has nine logical links to Tytsjerksteradiel, Westerkwartier, Opsterland and Achtkarspelen. Two A7 records share NWB-road-7, two N31 records share NWB-road-31 and three N358 records share NWB-road-358; each family is one series corridor, never independent capacity.
Distances 0.100–3.136 km and nominal 150/260 values describe boundary geometry and scenario-unit ceilings, not route length, lanes, vehicles per hour, evacuation throughput or responder travel time.

No ProRail station lies inside GM0090; 82 GTFS stop areas include Drachten Transferium Oost, Van Knobelsdorffplein and Ziekenhuis. Schedule/register presence is not live service, accessible vehicles, drivers, fuel, road passability or evacuation capacity.

Nij Smellinghe lies inside Drachten and reports a 24/7 emergency department, acute obstetrics, eight rooms and 13,398 visits in 2025. The annual survey does not establish incident-time acceptance, staffing, occupancy, utilities, backup/fuel, oxygen/medicine, surge or road access.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland, Stichting Mijn Aansluiting, RDI, DUO, KNMI, RIVM, Rijkswaterstaat and NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public lifeline planning/register layers and scoped current NoData
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment/public queries retrieved 2–3 September 2026; licences and cadence remain source-specific
supports: A live responsibility-area query at the municipal reference point returns Liander for electricity (record updated 24 March 2026) and gas (17 December 2025), Vitens for water and Ziggo for media (both 7 September 2025), and no drainage record. Public Domain territories are provider context, not topology, connectivity, coverage quality, live service or restoration.

One postcode sample 9216WE maps to Liander area OS DRACHTEN 10-1i and reports planning fields: withdrawal existing 45 MW, required 63 MW, queue 14.4 MW/20 requests; injection existing 90 MW, required 71 MW, queue 20 MW/29 requests; six projects, earliest 2027. It is not current load, outage, reserve or a municipal total; the exact open-data licence identifier was not found.

RDI assigns 131 antenna sites representing 248 antennas, including 49 mobile-communication and 24 fixed-link sites; DUO assigns 60 education locations. RDI's service states no exact reuse licence and DUO labels CC BY without version. Neither supplies coverage/backhaul/power nor occupancy/shelter capacity.

The deployment assigns zero local NDW situations, KNMI weather stations, RIVM PM2.5 stations, Waterinfo observations/forecasts and 365-day KNMI seismic-event origins. Empty/no-match is NoData, never open roads, normal local conditions, zero seismic hazard or safety.

identity.summary: GM0090, Smallingerland, Fryslân and Veiligheidsregio Fryslân agree across generated and official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature ID, bundle code/name, province and safety-region membership are coherent.
The reference point lies inside official generalized geometry.
Annual administrative edition, publication/retrieval time, observation/forecast validity and synthetic exercise time remain distinct.

geography.summary: Administrative containment is coherent, but Drachten, boezem/polder country and the Alde Feanen/Hegewarren peat edge require distinct exposure mechanics.
notes: Use full geometry for evidence containment; the generalized boundary and municipal centre are overview controls only.
Mainland dike-ring-6 flooding, polder-dike failure, boezem pressure, rainfall nuisance and nature fire are separate mechanisms.
Neighbourhood, BAG place, BRT settlement, defence/compartment, water-control point and scenario eligibility cannot be collapsed into one scalar.

demography.summary: The 57,084 municipal control and 61 neighbourhood rows reconcile within normal CBS rounding.
notes: Neighbourhood population is 57,080, four below the control (-0.007%); households total 25,920 and rounded age-65-plus rows 12,895.
The simulator allocates back to the official municipal control without treating the rounding difference as missing people.
Annual residents omit hospital patients/staff, pupils, commuters, visitors, water recreation users, transient road users and responders.

regionalDetail.summary: All 61 neighbourhoods are retained, but partial statistics and within-neighbourhood hazard/service exposure remain unresolved.
notes: District heating and charging are absent in 61/61 rows; cars per household is absent in six and several housing/benefit fields in one or two.
Published nulls stay NoData; annual age, household, home, business and distance fields do not provide individual need or event-time presence.
Water, education, antenna and hospital records have separate coverage and cannot fill demographic or operational gaps.

settlements.summary: Fourteen BAG places and 28 BRT features preserve Drachten and the distributed village structure without assigning emergency roles.
notes: All retained BAG place centres are inside the generalized 2025 boundary.
BRT types are nine buurtschappen, six gehuchten and thirteen woonkernen.
A village, education building or ordinary community location is not an emergency support point; the official current count of the latter is zero.

transport.summary: Static A7/N-road and bus context is traceable, but common corridors, local bridges, live passability and hospital/evacuation throughput are Unknown.
notes: Nine boundary links span five route families; repeated A7, N31 and N358 edges are three non-additive series corridors.
There is no in-boundary ProRail station and 82 scheduled stop areas do not prove incident-time bus service.
Nij Smellinghe, evacuation, supply and mutual aid require event-valid local roads/bridges, vehicles, destination acceptance and current capacity; zero NDW matches is NoData.

emergencyContext.summary: Official planning supports mainland, polder, rainfall, fire and lifeline risk, but no live event/resource/action state is selected and current support-point capacity is zero.
notes: Regional scenarios and programmes establish plausible mechanisms and responsibilities, not current incidents, probabilities or GM0090 consequences.
The municipal zero emergency-support-point count is exact administrative evidence; proposed sites remain planned.
No support staff/stock, household preparedness, alert acknowledgement, evacuation capacity, hospital status, mutual aid or operator restoration is consumed.

notes: Initial focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 35.60 seconds, tests 35.29 seconds.
Diagnostic enumeration passed in 14.48 seconds; the controlled Alde Feanen source test passed separately in 0.42 seconds.
Final focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 29.56 seconds, tests 29.34 seconds.
Execution coverage is not physical, operational or recovery calibration.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, reconciliation, determinism, service arithmetic and cumulative-burden invariants hold.
notes: Availability stays in [0,1], web/core factories agree, repeated runs are exact, demand/delivery reconcile and burden is monotonic.
T+24 values include 0.167350 pluvial, 0 major-river, 0.506396 coastal and 0.900759 compound severity; six decimals are synthetic precision.
A mathematically valid exercise remains distinct from an observation, forecast, official event, operator state or confirmed action.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Generic coastal/pluvial fields and population-led fire allocation do not represent Smallingerland's dike-ring, polder, drainage and nature geography.
notes: Major-river T+24/T+72 reports zero depth and affected, consistent with absence of a Rhine/Meuse/IJssel direct pathway; retain this direct-impact suppression but do not label the municipality safe.
Coastal T+24 reports 1.339531 m and 23,038 affected without a selected dike-ring-6 breach, defence condition, LIWO-connected footprint, arrival, duration or recession.
Pluvial T+24 reports 0.231716 m and 2,539 affected, led by population leaders without event rainfall, terrain, sewer, groundwater, boezem/polder or water-control state.
A controlled Alde Feanen-edge source yields 0.457886 fire and 0.587114 smoke, yet large Drachten neighbourhoods lead impact rather than source geography.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight balances calculate, but managed water, utilities, multimodal access, hospital continuity, communications and supplies lack operational topology/state.
notes: Earthquake T+24 reports zero ground motion but 5,106 affected, all eight services below one and 231,725 cumulative person-hours; no causal initiating impact supports this burden.

Compound T+24 availability is power 0.440714, water 0.522586, drainage 0.460680, gas 0.683647, telecom 0.336954, mobility 0.564600, facilities 0.481332 and supply 0.468850; these exact values have no operator validation.

The 375 water points, provider territories, grid sample, 131 antennas, 60 schools, roads/stops and annual hospital survey do not supply connectivity, flow/load/quality/control, backup, staff, vehicles, stocks or restoration.
NWB informs Mobility and assumed road-logistics Supply only; it is never electricity, water, drainage, gas, telecom or facility topology.

causalTrace.summary: Synthetic ledgers close, but missing event geometry, local exposure, lifeline state and confirmed actions do not gate consequences.
notes: No selected input supplies dike-ring/polder defence failure, connected flood footprint, event rainfall, sewer/groundwater/peil/control state, fire perimeter/wind/fuel, earthquake motion, cyber target, operator outage or hospital acceptance.
The zero-motion earthquake impact is an explicit internal contradiction, while coastal, pluvial and compound exactness lacks locality-specific external causation.
Official scenario, programme, partial register, annual survey, planning sample, current observation and synthetic model state must retain separate evidence classes and valid times.
Unsupported exact values must render synthetic screening/Unknown; no-match and expired data cannot become zero, normal, open or safe.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 classifications and restoration curves are not governed by Smallingerland actions, operator milestones, hospital continuity or support capacity.
notes: Storm, pluvial, winter, cyber and earthquake show zero thresholded affected and an operational label at T+72 while cumulative burdens reach 725,152; 317,308; 752,017; 767,734; and 386,327 person-hours and residual service deficits remain.
Coastal depth falls to zero by T+72 while 2,764 remain affected and burden reaches 1,771,984; the unsourced impact/recovery path is not an authority all-clear.
Compound depth remains 0.388837, affected rises 29,924 to 30,500 and burden reaches 2,109,432; all eight services worsen without confirmed action/resource state.
A 72-hour household-preparedness horizon and future support points are not restoration promises; only valid, authorized and confirmed actions may change recovery.

findings.summary: Official identity, demographic reconciliation, places and settlement membership are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 confirms GM0090, 57,084 residents, 61 neighbourhoods, fourteen BAG places and 28 BRT features; the four-person neighbourhood difference is -0.007% and null fields remain NoData.
findings.action: Retain code/name checks, boundary containment, official controls, source edition/licence, field-level coverage and deterministic reconciliation.

findings.summary: The major-river preset correctly suppresses unsupported direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel impact in Smallingerland.
findings.evidence: At T+24 and T+72 river depth, affected residents and burden are zero. E02 lists mainland and polder flooding but not a major-river pathway.
findings.action: Retain zero direct major-river forcing for GM0090. Label unmodelled cross-boundary supply, mutual-aid or displacement effects Unknown rather than safe or impossible.

findings.summary: A generic coastal scalar substitutes for two authority-defined flood pathways.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 emits 1.339531 m and 23,038 affected. E02 supports a selected dike-ring-6 mainland breach and a separate wind/rain/high-boezem polder-dike failure, neither a municipality-wide analytic depth.
findings.action: Suppress exact direct coastal consequences until a governed event selects mainland or polder mechanism and supplies defence/breach, connected footprint, depth, arrival, duration and recession; retain official eligibility as context.

findings.summary: Exact rain-flood depth and allocation ignore Drachten's ageing sewer and Smallingerland's managed water system.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports 0.231716 m and 2,539 affected without event rainfall, terrain, sewer, groundwater, boezem, peil or control state. E05 identifies 141 km planned for replacement; E04 has 375 non-causal register points.
findings.action: Bind a licensed stress surface and explicit rain event to AHN/BGT/BRO, sewer/catchment condition, groundwater, boezem/polders and valid pump/weir/sluice modes before publishing local depth or affected values.

findings.summary: The earthquake preset generates people and service consequences with zero ground motion.
findings.evidence: At T+24 groundMotionG and hazard severity are zero, yet 5,106 residents remain affected, every service is degraded and cumulative burden is 231,725 person-hours. No local KNMI event origin exists in the scoped 365-day catalogue, which is NoData rather than zero hazard.
findings.action: When event-attributable ground motion is zero, suppress earthquake damage, affected people and recovery burden. Any induced/natural fixture must name origin, magnitude/depth, issue/valid time, motion/intensity surface and exposure/vulnerability model.

findings.summary: Official nature-fire eligibility is not translated into source-contained land-cover-aware exposure.
findings.evidence: E03/E06 establish Alde Feanen reed, peat, marsh woodland and recreation context. A controlled local source produces 3,928 affected but population-dominant Drachten neighbourhoods lead rather than source-adjacent areas.
findings.action: Require ignition/perimeter, eligible combustible cover, fuel/moisture, current wind/plume, recreation occupancy, access, firewater, crews and suppression state; otherwise show synthetic municipal eligibility with local distribution Unknown.

findings.summary: A partial managed-water/wastewater register is absent from causal drainage and flood recovery.
findings.evidence: E04 assigns 375 points, including 60 surface pumps, eight sewer pumps and rwzi Drachten, but 333 capacities are null and no catchment/control/power/backup/flow state enters the model.
findings.action: Keep register points contextual. Add authority-reviewed catchments, comparable units, flow direction, control mode, energy/backup, maintenance and valid-time operation before any point changes Water or Drainage.

findings.summary: Nij Smellinghe and dispersed settlements depend on unverified common corridors, local access and live destination capacity.
findings.evidence: E07 verifies non-additive A7/N31/N358 series, no rail station and 82 scheduled bus stops. Nij Smellinghe is an in-municipality acute-care anchor, but annual offer and road geometry do not prove incident-time access or acceptance.
findings.action: Model event-valid local roads/bridges and common corridors, closures, vehicle/mode capacity, hospital acceptance/diversion, staff and critical supplies; zero NDW and static GTFS stay NoData/context.

findings.summary: Public utility, antenna, education and grid-planning records cannot calibrate eight operational services.
findings.evidence: E08 identifies Liander/Vitens/Ziggo territories, one planning sample, 131 antenna sites and 60 education locations, but no complete topology, live state, priority, backup, stock, crew or restoration estimate; centre drainage is empty.
findings.action: Expose publisher/version/time/coverage/licence/evidence class and affectsSimulation=false. Use releasable operator aggregates or transparent synthetic assumptions, with unavailable state explicitly Unknown.

findings.summary: Zero current emergency support points and missing actions invalidate implied first-72-hour support and recovery.
findings.evidence: E05 states there are currently no support points and locations are being prepared. Several presets become operational with zero thresholded affected at T+72 despite residual deficits and burdens up to 767,734 person-hours; compound worsens.
findings.action: Render zero current support points as an administrative fact, proposed sites as planned, and add an authorized T0–T+72 action/resource ledger for alerting, evacuation, hospital continuity, water, food, medicine, power, sanitation, communications, welfare and mutual aid.

corrections.summary: Retain GM0090 major-river suppression and replace generic coastal values with selected mainland/polder mechanisms.
corrections.validation: River direct depth/affected/burden remain zero at all six checkpoints while indirect effects render Unknown unless sourced. Mainland/polder outputs require mechanism, dike ring or polder/defence, breach/overtopping, LIWO-connected footprint, arrival, depth, duration, recession, version/licence and NoData; eligibility alone never generates municipal depth.

corrections.summary: Gate Smallingerland pluvial and nature-fire consequences on source-specific geography.
corrections.validation: Unsupported choropleths render Unknown. Pluvial fixtures bind licensed rainfall/stress, terrain, sewer/groundwater, boezem/polders and controls; a controlled Alde Feanen fire fixture contains the source and uses land cover/fuel/wind instead of population rank.

corrections.summary: Eliminate zero-motion earthquake consequences and preserve seismic NoData semantics.
corrections.validation: With groundMotionG=0, event-attributable earthquake damage, affected people, service loss and burden are zero. A nonzero fixture requires governed source and motion/intensity evidence; zero local catalogue origins remains NoData, never zero hazard.

corrections.summary: Represent water-chain, utility, communications, education and hospital records as contextual evidence without invented operation.
corrections.validation: The 375 partial water points, provider territories, NBNL sample, 131 antennas, 60 education locations and Nij Smellinghe show provenance/time/coverage/licence/evidence class. Null capacity and register status never imply current state; no context record changes service without explicit authorized binding.

corrections.summary: Make Smallingerland corridors, acute-care continuity and first-72-hour actions validity-bound.
corrections.validation: A7, N31 and N358 repeated edges each share one physical ceiling. Nij Smellinghe, evacuation and supply require valid access, mode/vehicle capacity and acceptance. Current support-point count displays zero; proposed sites remain planned, and only confirmed actions/resources change recovery with unresolved needs carried beyond T+72.

residualLimitations: No authority-selected Smallingerland dike-ring-6 or polder event supplies defence state, breach/overtopping, connected footprint, arrival, depth, duration or recession; major-river distance is not a substitute.
No complete versioned local rainfall, AHN/soil/groundwater, sewer, culvert, storage, peilgebied, receiving-water, pump/weir/sluice control or road-passability model is consumed.
HWH coverage is partial; 333 of 375 capacity values are null and the remaining values do not establish comparable units, connected catchments, operation, energy/backup, crew or reserve.
No event-valid Alde Feanen ignition, perimeter, complete combustible cover, fuel moisture, wind/smoke, visitor occupancy, access, firewater, crew or suppression state is consumed.

No operator-approved Liander feeder, Vitens pressure zone, gas, Ziggo/mobile backhaul, critical-customer, switching, live load/flow/quality, backup, crew or restoration topology is public and consumed.
NWB/GTFS establish geometry and schedule context only; no live local bridge/road/bus status, evacuation vehicle inventory or responder/hospital travel time is represented.
No live Nij Smellinghe acceptance, staffing, occupancy, utilities, backup/fuel, oxygen/blood/medicine, surge, supply or transfer state is represented.
The official current emergency-support-point count is zero; planned locations, ordinary community buildings and schools are not shelters or stocked operational sites.
Scenario outputs remain deterministic exercises, not current observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties, operator commitments or calibrated losses.
provinceReviewFlags: Across Fryslân, separate direct sea flooding, dike-ring-6 mainland flooding, polder-dike failure, boezem flooding, rainfall nuisance and Rhine/Meuse/IJssel high water; eligibility never substitutes for a connected footprint.

Build a governed Wetterskip adapter for polder/boezem compartments, defences, Hegewarren/Alde Feanen, pumps, weirs, sluices, wastewater and valid-time control while preserving partial coverage and NoData.

Replace common population-led neighbourhood allocation with source-specific rain, fire, wind, heat and cyber geography; retain official Smallingerland nature-fire eligibility without inventing an incident.
Treat repeated A7, N31 and N358 records as three non-additive series corridors and audit local bridge/access dependencies for Nij Smellinghe, evacuation, supply and mutual aid.
Keep Liander, Vitens, Ziggo, NBNL, antenna, education, hospital and transport registers contextual until current connectivity, capacity, backup and state are authorized and time-aligned.

Preserve Smallingerland's official zero emergency-support-point status and 141 km sewer-renewal programme as planning/condition evidence; 72 hours is an operations window, never guaranteed restoration.
